Numbering re-derived rather than assumed: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Psalm 120 rule identity, 7 WEB verses / 7 MT verses, web_title true, so the row's title pair web:Ps.120.0 = oshb:Ps.120.1 is arithmetically correct and every body cite is 1:1. Both title splices (שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת) collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.120.1; that string also stands byte-identically at oshb:Ps.123.1, oshb:Ps.125.1, oshb:Ps.126.1, oshb:Ps.128.1, oshb:Ps.129.1, oshb:Ps.132.1 and oshb:Ps.134.1 (8 verses book-wide, verse count, byte tier), so the splice is not psalm-unique but is byte-true for the ref it is bound to. The ascription-absence claim holds from the bytes: MT 120:1 carries neither the le-David token (לְדָ֫וִ֥ד, byte tier at oshb:Ps.122.1) nor a li-Shlomo token; a skeleton sweep of לדוד over the opening verses of Ps 120-131 returns 122, 124, 131 and not 120. WEB quotations are verbatim (check_web_quotes GREEN across the cluster: 24 quotes, 0 flags), and the peace/war antithesis the row rests its close on is real. What fails is the morphological and positional description of that antithesis in the second observed_substrate_signal, filed below. The signal is load-bearing - it is what the row uses to join the psalm's two closing verses into one move - so the defect is material even though the row's conclusion survives a corrected restatement. unit_type whole_psalm and high confidence are appropriate for a 7-verse psalm with no internal tier-1 seam.

challenges.claim: The second observed_substrate_signal grounds the 120:6|120:7 linkage in a shared 'closing verb's root', but the shared lexeme is a noun and it is not verse-closing in the 120:7 quote the signal itself cites.
challenges.evidence: MT 120:6 reads רַ֭בַּת שָֽׁכְנָה לָּ֣הּ נַפְשִׁ֑י עִ֝֗ם שׂוֹנֵ֥א שָׁלֽוֹם (collate.py tier byte against oshb:Ps.120.6); its verse-final word is שָׁלֽוֹם. MT 120:7, which the signal quotes in full, reads אֲֽנִי שָׁ֭לוֹם וְכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר הֵ֝֗מָּה לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (collate.py tier byte against oshb:Ps.120.7): the shared lexeme שָׁ֭לוֹם stands at word index 1 of 6, and the verse-final word is לַמִּלְחָמָֽה. The lexeme therefore closes only one of the two verses, so the signal's word 'closing' does not hold for the pair it describes. On part of speech, both witnesses read a noun, not a verb: “My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace.” (web:Ps.120.6) and “I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.” (web:Ps.120.7) - 'peace' in both, with 'war' closing the second. The staged extract carries no morphology layer (verse_map_oshb.json holds text/language/web only), so no verb reading is recoverable from the source; the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings settle it. No alternative reading rescues the wording either: the two verses' participial and finite forms (שׂוֹנֵ֥א at oshb:Ps.120.6, אֲדַבֵּ֑ר at oshb:Ps.120.7) share no root. The repair is a restatement, not a driver swap - the shared noun is byte-true in both verses and still carries the row's close.

reviews.reasoning: Every quantified claim in this row re-derives exactly, which is worth recording as such. Numbering first: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Psalm 121 rule identity, 8 WEB / 8 MT verses, so web:Ps.121.0 = oshb:Ps.121.1 is correct and the body cites are 1:1; the span tiles the psalm. The title-spelling contrast is byte-true and book-unique: a sweep of שִׁ֗יר לַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת over verse_map_oshb.json returns exactly 1 verse book-wide (oshb:Ps.121.1) at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton tiers alike, while the skeleton form המעלות stands in the opening verse of 11 of the 12 psalms in Ps 120-131 and למעלות in exactly 1, Psalm 121. The row's 'sweep: 12 titles in Ps 120-131, 1 exception at Psalm 121' reproduces digit for digit, and 'this part's other eleven titled psalms' is the correct complement (the strategy sets this writer part at Ps 120-131, so the part scoping is right too). The keep/guard ladder also reproduces: a skeleton sweep of the 3-letter form returns 69 verses book-wide - the row's figure - and hits exactly oshb:Ps.121.3, oshb:Ps.121.5, oshb:Ps.121.7, oshb:Ps.121.8 inside the psalm; the with-mater form returns 3 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.121.4, oshb:Ps.127.1, oshb:Ps.145.20), again the row's figure - five of eight verses, as stated, with the unit named. Each of the five spliced fragments collates at byte tier against a ref the row cites. The row correctly demotes the ladder to corroboration rather than driver, matching the strategy's treatment of the ascents' step-parallelism as texture. The cross-psalm cite oshb:Ps.120.1 is mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs (check_refs_mirror GREEN). Addressee continuity holds in both witnesses: web:Ps.121.3 through web:Ps.121.8 carry second-person suffixes with no vocative and no independent pronoun intervening. No selah, paseq or K/Q note falls in Ps.121.* (pmarks_Ps.json), so nothing is under-disclosed. OBSERVATION, not a defect: the fourth ladder fragment (יְֽהוָ֗ה יִשְׁמָר) collates at byte tier against BOTH oshb:Ps.121.7 and oshb:Ps.121.8, being also a prefix of MT 121:7's opening; the row cites both refs so the binding is unambiguous, but a future re-cut should prefer a discriminating fragment. OBSERVATION: 'in two spellings' collapses a participle and an imperfect into a spelling contrast; the claim is nonetheless true as stated at skeleton tier, which is the tier the row names.

Numbering re-derived: Psalm 122 is rule identity with 9 WEB / 9 MT verses, so web:Ps.122.0 = oshb:Ps.122.1 is correct and the span tiles the psalm. The title splice שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.122.1, and the le-David count is exactly right: a skeleton sweep of לדוד over the opening verses of Ps 120-131 returns 3 psalms - 122, 124, 131 - the row's list verbatim. (The same sweep across the full ascents 120-134 returns 5, adding 132 and 133, but the row scopes its count to the part and the part is Ps 120-131, so the scoping is sound.) The mood-shift reading at web:Ps.122.6 is fair and whole_psalm is policy-compliant; there is no rival tier-1 seam in the psalm. The defect is count discipline rather than segmentation: the row twice asserts a universal about the psalm's subject and backs it with a refs list carrying no count and no named unit. The underlying fact is narrower than the wording, so the challenge is filed at low severity - the conclusion is defensible once the claim is scoped and swept.

challenges.claim: The rationale asserts twice that Jerusalem is the psalm's subject 'throughout' with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep and no named unit, and the supporting signal lists three refs without a count; the proper noun in fact stands in 3 of the psalm's 9 verses.
challenges.evidence: A skeleton sweep of ירושלם (spliced from the verse-final token of oshb:Ps.122.2) over verse_map_oshb.json returns 3 verses inside Psalm 122 - oshb:Ps.122.2, oshb:Ps.122.3, oshb:Ps.122.6 - and 17 verses book-wide (verse counts, not token counts). WEB agrees exactly: a case-folded phrase sweep over verse_map_web.json returns the same 3 verses, “Our feet are standing within your gates, Jerusalem!” (web:Ps.122.2), “Jerusalem is built as a city that is compact together,” (web:Ps.122.3), and “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Those who love you will prosper.” (web:Ps.122.6). The six verses that do not name the city name other subjects, among them “For there are set thrones for judgment, the thrones of David's house.” (web:Ps.122.5) and “For the sake of the house of Yahweh our God, I will seek your good.” (web:Ps.122.9). check_universals.py flags this row's rationale at both occurrences of the universal, and they are the only substantive universals it flags in the cluster. The continuity the row actually wants is carried by the second-person feminine suffixes running web:Ps.122.6-web:Ps.122.9, which the row never cites; that, plus '3 of 9 verses name the city (verse count)', is the swept form of the same claim.

challenges.claim: The first observed_substrate_signal argues a title-ascription contrast against another psalm without mirroring the compared verse oshb:Ps.122.1 in boundary_evidence_refs, breaking the practice this same writer follows on identical contrasts elsewhere in the part.
challenges.evidence: The contrast rests entirely on bytes outside the span: MT 122:1's title carries לְדָ֫וִ֥ד at word index 2 (collate.py tier byte against oshb:Ps.122.1), where MT 123:1's title stops at שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת (byte tier against oshb:Ps.123.1). The fact is correct - a skeleton sweep of לדוד over the opening verses of Ps 120-131 returns 122, 124 and 131 and not 123 - but this row's boundary_evidence_refs holds Ps 123 refs only, so the evidence for half the comparison is uncited. check_refs_mirror.py returns GREEN and structurally cannot do otherwise: its resolution arms cover Ps.C.V tokens, bare C:V colon cites, 'MT c:v' qualifiers, and bare 'verse N' inside the span psalm, none of which fires on a psalm-level mention carrying no verse number. A book-wide byte sweep of the three-word summons returns exactly 2 verses, oshb:Ps.124.1 and oshb:Ps.129.1 (accent_stripped 2; skeleton 3, adding oshb:Ps.118.2 where the accents differ) - so 'byte-identical (3 of 3 words match)' is exactly right, and the row is also right to keep the relation as disclosed texture rather than a merge, which is the settled treatment for typed relations. The maker-formula splice likewise collates at byte tier against both oshb:Ps.124.8 and oshb:Ps.121.2. Three positional and distributional statements wrapped around those correct byte facts do not survive the bytes, and I file them below. None of them moves the span: the eight verses have no rival tier-1 seam, the lament-to-blessing turn at web:Ps.124.6 is correctly read as the conditional's own resolution, and whole_psalm at high confidence stands. No selah, paseq or K/Q note falls in Ps.124.* (pmarks_Ps.json); check_web_quotes returns the WEB quotations verbatim; the cross-psalm refs are mirrored (check_refs_mirror GREEN).

challenges.claim: The rationale calls the maker-of-heaven-and-earth formula the same formula 'that ends Psalm 121'; it ends MT and WEB 121:2, and Psalm 121 ends six verses later.
challenges.evidence: The formula עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ occupies words 3-5 of the 6-word MT 121:2 (collate.py tier byte against oshb:Ps.121.2), so it closes that verse and nothing larger. web_mt_offset_map.json gives Psalm 121 rule identity with 8 WEB and 8 MT verses, and the psalm's last verse is “Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.” (web:Ps.121.8), MT 121:8 closing on עוֹלָֽם (byte tier against oshb:Ps.121.8). The row's own second observed_substrate_signal states the fact correctly as the closing formula of Psalm 121:2, so the rationale contradicts its own signal. That the distinction is available to the writer is visible one psalm later, where the parallel claim at web:Ps.125.5 is stated correctly as at the close of Psalm 128 - MT 128:6 genuinely is the last of Psalm 128's 6 verses, and שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל collates at byte tier against both oshb:Ps.125.5 and oshb:Ps.128.6.

challenges.claim: Both of the row's 'opens' claims for the Israel-summons are positionally false: the clause is verse-final in MT 124:1 and verse-final in MT 129:1, opening neither psalm's body.
challenges.evidence: MT 124:1 splices word by word (collate.py tier byte against oshb:Ps.124.1) as title at words 0-2, then לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ at words 3-6, then the summons יֹֽאמַר נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at words 7-9 - verse-final, following the protasis, not opening the body. WEB carries the same order: “If it had not been Yahweh who was on our side, let Israel now say,” (web:Ps.124.1). MT 129:1 runs title at words 0-1, רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרַ֑י at words 2-4, and the summons יֹֽאמַר נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at words 5-7 (byte tier against oshb:Ps.129.1) - so the clause closes 129:1, and Psalm 129's body opens with a different clause entirely. The discourse point the row is reaching for (the summons introduces the speech resumed at web:Ps.124.2) is available and defensible, but it has to be stated as a discourse function rather than as linear position, and 'the same clause opening Psalm 129' has no reading that survives the word order.

challenges.claim: The maker-formula signal characterizes the byte-identical tag's distribution as spanning two parents with no occurrence count; a book-wide byte sweep returns four verses, of which the row names two.
challenges.evidence: A byte sweep of עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ over verse_map_oshb.json returns 4 verses: oshb:Ps.115.15, oshb:Ps.121.2, oshb:Ps.124.8, oshb:Ps.134.3 (accent_stripped 4; skeleton 5, adding oshb:Ps.146.6) - verse counts, not token counts. The row names oshb:Ps.121.2 and oshb:Ps.124.8 only. The signal's only digit, '3 of 3 words match', counts words in the string rather than verses carrying it, so the distributional claim ships with no unit-bearing count at all. The contrast with the row's other signal is instructive: the summons claim is complete, because the byte sweep there really does return exactly the 2 verses named.

reviews.reasoning: Psalm 125 is rule identity, 5 WEB / 5 MT verses; web:Ps.125.0 = oshb:Ps.125.1 is correct and the span tiles the psalm. All three Hebrew splices collate at byte tier against the refs cited: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת and צִיּ֥וֹן לֹא against oshb:Ps.125.1, סָבִ֪יב לָ֥הּ וַ֭יהוָה סָבִ֣יב against oshb:Ps.125.2, and the closing tag שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל against oshb:Ps.125.5. The byte-identity claim verifies exactly, and unlike the parallel claim one psalm earlier its distribution statement is complete: a book-wide byte sweep of that three-word tag returns exactly 2 verses, oshb:Ps.125.5 and oshb:Ps.128.6, at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton tiers alike (verse counts) - so naming two psalms is the whole book-wide picture, not a subset. The positional claim is exact too: the tag occupies words 3-5 of the 6-word MT 128:6, which is the last of Psalm 128's 6 verses, so 'at the close of Psalm 128' is byte-true. No selah, paseq or K/Q note falls in Ps.125.* (pmarks_Ps.json); check_web_quotes returns the WEB quotations verbatim including the elided-prefix form at web:Ps.125.5; check_refs_mirror mirrors web:Ps.128.6. The simile-statement-imperative reading is a fair description of the five verses and no tier-1 signal argues an internal seam, so whole_psalm at high confidence stands. OBSERVATION, not a defect: the gloss on the second splice reads with an internal ellipsis, but the quoted bytes are contiguous - words 2-5 of MT 125:2, with nothing elided between them - so the ellipsis marks an omission that does not exist. Quote and gloss do cover the same span, which is what the parity rule requires; the ellipsis is a cosmetic desync worth re-cutting in an author wave rather than a challengeable evidence defect.

Psalm 126 is rule identity, 6 WEB / 6 MT verses; web:Ps.126.0 = oshb:Ps.126.1 is correct and the span tiles the psalm. All four Hebrew splices collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.126.1 and oshb:Ps.126.4 as cited. The ketiv/qere disclosure is the row's strongest element and it verifies against both the inventory and the bytes: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries 65 refs, one of which is Ps.126.4, and MT 126:4 splices as שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת שבותנו שְׁבִיתֵ֑נוּ ... - word index 3 is the unpointed inline ketiv (codepoints U+05E9 U+05D1 U+05D5 U+05EA U+05E0 U+05D5, no points on any of them) and word index 4 the pointed qere, exactly the inline-ketiv configuration the toolkit warns about and exactly as the row states it. The row also correctly declines to select a reading. The shared-root link across the mood shift is byte-true in both directions and is the right warrant for holding the psalm together. Confidence 'medium' is the one calibrated confidence in this cluster and it is earned: the rejected_alternative names the web:Ps.126.3 / web:Ps.126.4 mood change as a genuine rival rather than a formality, which is honest for a psalm whose only internal candidate seam sits exactly there. No selah or paseq falls in Ps.126.* (pmarks_Ps.json); check_web_quotes returns the WEB quotations verbatim, including the two-verse elided form at web:Ps.126.5-web:Ps.126.6. OBSERVATION, not a defect: citation_sweep.py raises one WARN on this row - the Hebrew quote in the first observed_substrate_signal binds to K/Q verse oshb:Ps.126.4 with no ketiv/qere disclosure in-field. The disclosure exists and is correct, but in the next signal, so the requirement is met at row level and missed at field level. OBSERVATION: that same first signal quotes two words (שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה, byte tier) and glosses three elements; the third glossed element corresponds to the K/Q pair at word indices 3-4, which the trailing ellipsis does signpost - but a gloss reaching bytes the quote does not carry is the expansion side of the quote/gloss parity rule. Re-cutting the quote to carry the K/Q token in-field would resolve both observations in a single edit.
